info.title: FoleyTimePro TimeClock API
info.description:
The **read-only external reporting / BI surface** of FoleyTimePro TimeClock.

This API exists so a payroll system, a BI tool (Power BI, a spreadsheet import,
a QuickBooks sync), or a compliance dashboard can pull time, schedule, time-off
and geofence data out of this installation without touching the admin UI. It is
deliberately **read-only** today: every endpoint is a `GET`, and the write
scopes visible in the key-creation form (`punches:write`, `timeoff:write`,
`employees:write`) are reserved for a future revision and are honored by
nothing yet.

### Authentication
Every endpoint (including discovery) requires a valid API key sent as
`Authorization: Bearer <64-hex-char-key>`. Keys are created in
**Admin → API Keys**, are scoped to exactly the data an integration needs, and
are rate-limited to 60 requests/minute. See the `ApiKeyBearer` security scheme
below for the full contract.

### The response envelope
Every JSON response — success or error — is `{"success": true|false, ...}`.
A row-listing endpoint's payload is `data.rows` (or, for the two endpoints with
an older, stable public contract, `data.employees` / `data.punches`) alongside
a `data.meta` block describing exactly what was applied: the effective
date range, filters, rounding/overtime rules, pagination, and a `warnings`
array that calls out anything that could make a number misleading (a partial
week, an open punch, a page that doesn't cover the full result set, and so on).
Read `data.meta.warnings` before trusting a headline total.

### CSV export
Every row-listing endpoint except `/punches` and `/meta` accepts
`format=csv` and streams a UTF-8 (with BOM) CSV instead of the JSON envelope.
CSV has nowhere to put `meta`, so the handful of fields an unattended importer
needs (timezone, row/total counts, has_more, warnings) are mirrored into
`X-Report-*` response headers instead of being silently dropped.

### Consistency across the surface
Every report that computes worked hours (`/reports/hours`, `/summary`,
`/overtime`, `/utilization`, `/attendance`, `/payroll`, `/trends`) recomputes
them from the raw punch `TIME` columns through the same shared calculator —
`timepunches.TotalHours` is never trusted, because one insert path writes a
literal `0` and admin edits do not always recompute it. Rounding is always
applied once, to the summed day, before overtime is allocated from the rounded
figures — this is what keeps `/summary`, `/overtime`, `/utilization`,
`/payroll` and `/trends` from ever disagreeing about the same employee's same
day.

servers.description: Production (the only environment this installation serves).

tags.name: Discovery
tags.description: Self-discovery: confirm an API key is valid and see exactly what it can reach — its own scopes, the full endpoint catalog, current server limits, and how much data actually exists — before spending a request on an endpoint the key may not be scoped for.

tags.name: Employees
tags.description: The employee roster dimension: names, office, job title, active shift and current clock status, for mapping an external system's employees onto timeclock IDs and emails.

tags.name: Offices
tags.description: The office/location dimension, with total and active employee headcounts per office — including data-quality diagnostics for offices that exist only as free text on an employee record.

tags.name: Schedule
tags.description: Shift definitions (the rule set: days, span, lunch, grace period) and the expanded per-employee, per-date schedule derived from them, for scheduled-vs-actual joins against punches.

tags.name: Time Off
tags.description: The raw time-off request feed — one row per request, unfolded and unclipped, with a delta-sync cursor. For apportioned/aggregated time-off analytics see the Reports tag's `/reports/timeoff`.

tags.name: Punches
tags.description: Raw clock in/out and lunch punches with a delta-sync cursor, so an external system can own its own overtime math instead of trusting a derived total.

tags.name: Reports
tags.description: Aggregated hours, overtime, utilization, attendance, time-off, leave balances, payroll, data-quality exceptions, punctuality, trend and geofence compliance reporting — the BI surface of this API. Every report shares the same query-parameter contract (see the `start`/`end`/`rounding`/`ot_*` parameters below) so a date range, a rounding policy or an overtime rule means exactly the same thing no matter which report you call.

get.summary: Discover this key's scopes and the API's current limits
get.description:
Confirms an API key is valid and reports exactly what it can reach: the
key's own name/scopes/expiry, the full endpoint catalog (path, method,
required scope, one-line description), the server's current rate/range/
page-size limits, and a snapshot of how much data actually exists
(earliest/latest punch date, employee count).

**No scope is required** — this is the one endpoint any valid, unrevoked,
unexpired key may call regardless of which scopes it holds, so an
integration can always self-diagnose "is my key even working" before
touching a scoped endpoint.

`tz`/`format` are the only query parameters honored; `format` is accepted
(never reported in `ignored_params`) but has no effect — there is no
tabular data on this endpoint for CSV to export, so the response is
always JSON.

`endpoints` is a hand-maintained catalog kept in the endpoint's own code
rather than generated from the router, specifically so a route that is
scaffolded but not yet wired never appears here as though it were
callable — treat it as authoritative over guessing from a scope name.

200.description: Key info, endpoint catalog, server limits and a data snapshot.

endpoints.description: Fact table: one row per employee per day with punch activity.

get.description:
The employee roster, for mapping an external system's own employees onto
timeclock IDs / emails.

**Backward compatibility note:** this is the original external-API
endpoint and its response keys (`id` as a **string**, `email`,
`first_name`, `last_name`, `office`, `active`) keep their exact legacy
names, types and meaning even though every newer report endpoint on this
surface emits integer employee IDs. The payload lives at
`data.employees` (not `data.rows`) for the same reason.

`include_inactive` **defaults to `true` here**, unlike every other
endpoint on this API (which default to `false`): today this endpoint
returns every employee, locked out or not, with no filter at all, and
flipping that default would silently drop employees from an existing
integration's sync.

`has_schedule` / `shift_id` / `shift_name` reflect only an **active**
shift assignment, matching `/schedule` and `/reports/utilization` exactly
— this endpoint can never disagree with those about whether an employee
currently has a schedule. `clock_status` folds the internal 3-value
`In`/`Lunch`/`Out` state down to the 2-value `In`/`Out` (`Lunch` counts as
`In`); `null` means "never punched," which is a different fact from
`Out` and is reported as such. The kiosk badge ID (`TagID`) is never
exposed by this or any endpoint.

parameters.name: include_inactive
parameters.description: Include locked-out employees. Defaults to **true** on this endpoint only (every other endpoint on this API defaults to false) — see the description above.

200.description: The employee roster matching the filters.

get.summary: List the office/location dimension with headcounts
get.description:
The office/location dimension for a BI star schema: every office an
employee or report row can join against, with total and active headcounts
attached.

`users.Office` is a free-text column with **no foreign key** to
`Offices` — nothing stops a typo, a renamed office, or a bulk import from
leaving employees pointing at a name with no matching `Offices` row.
Those orphan names are still returned as rows (with `office_id: null`)
rather than silently dropped, because dropping them would make this
endpoint's headcounts disagree with `/employees` with no way for an
integrator to see why; `meta.warnings` names up to 10 of them. Employees
with no office at all get no row (there is no dimension member to give
them) but are counted in `meta.employees_without_office` /
`active_employees_without_office` so `rows` plus that figure reconciles
to the full roster. If `Offices` itself has two rows sharing a name, both
appear and each reports the *same* employees — `meta.warnings` flags this
so a naive sum doesn't double count.

This is a dimension, not a time series: no date range and no
`include_inactive` (every row already reports both a total and an
active-only count).

totals.description: Totals for the returned page of offices only.

get.description:
The shift **rule set**: every shift definition — days it runs, span,
lunch, grace period, auto-clock-out — with the hours a single day of it
is worth. `/schedule` expands these rules onto a calendar; this endpoint
is the rule set itself, so a BI model can label a schedule row without
re-deriving anything.

`scheduled_hours_per_day` is the shift's span (end minus start, rolling
past midnight for an overnight shift) minus its lunch duration, computed
by forcing the shift to run every day of the week — it is a property of
the span, not of any one calendar date.

`shifts.DaysOfWeek` is stored as a JSON array inside a `VARCHAR` with
nothing enforcing its shape. A value that fails to decode, or that names
a day outside Mon–Sun, yields `days_of_week: []` (or a trimmed partial
list) plus a `meta.warnings` entry naming the shift — a shift that
quietly schedules nobody is exactly the kind of defect this response
surfaces rather than hides.

`include_inactive` here governs the **shift's** `IsActive` flag, not any
employee's status, and defaults to `false`.

parameters.name: include_inactive
parameters.description: Include shifts whose `IsActive` flag is not 1.

totals.description: Totals for the returned page of shifts only.

get.summary: List the expanded per-employee, per-date schedule
get.description:
The **expanded** schedule: one row per employee per scheduled date inside
`[start, end]`. `/shifts` is the rule set; this endpoint applies that rule
set to a calendar so a BI model can do "scheduled vs. actual" by joining
against `/punches` on `(employee_id, date)` without re-deriving
`DaysOfWeek`, overnight spans or lunch deductions itself.

An employee contributes a row only for a date that both falls inside the
range **and** is named in their one active assigned shift's
`DaysOfWeek`. An employee with no active shift (`has_schedule=false` on
`/employees`) contributes **no rows at all** — that is the correct,
expected result for this dimension expansion, not something to chase;
`meta.warnings` states how many such employees were excluded.

`scheduled_hours` is the shift's own rule for that date and is reported
**even on a date covered by approved time off** — this endpoint answers
"what did the shift say," and `is_working_day` / `time_off_type` is the
separate overlay answering "did leave override that." A consumer who
wants the netted figure can compute `scheduled_hours * is_working_day`
themselves; `/reports/utilization` does exactly that for its own
denominator.

`totals` describes the **entire filtered, date-expanded result**, not
just the returned page.

200.description: The expanded schedule for the requested range.

totals.description: Totals for the entire filtered, date-expanded result (not just the page).

get.summary: List the raw time-off request feed
get.description:
The **raw** time-off request feed — one row per request, unfolded and
unclipped. This is deliberately the opposite of `/reports/timeoff`, which
apportions hours across a range and folds requests up by employee: this
endpoint hands back the request records themselves so an external system
can own its own aggregation.

`start`/`end` here are an **optional overlap filter**
(`StartDate <= end AND EndDate >= start`), independently optional —
passing only one bounds that side and leaves the other open — because the
primary sync mechanism is `updated_since`, not a date window.

`updated_since` must be ISO 8601 **with an explicit UTC offset** (e.g.
`2026-07-20T08:00:00-05:00` or `...Z`) — without one the parse would
silently fall back to server-default time and a delta cursor would
quietly drift. It matches `COALESCE(ReviewedAt, RequestedAt)`, so a
review action re-surfaces a request even if it was already synced when
first submitted; rows are ordered by that same field so paging forward
with a rising `updated_since` walks the feed in true update order.

This endpoint does **not** accept `include_inactive` — the underlying
user filter defaults to active-employees-only with no way to widen it
here, so requests belonging to a since-locked-out employee are excluded.

No `totals` block: like `/punches`, this is a raw row feed, not an
aggregate.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Comma list over `Pending`, `Approved`, `Rejected` (case-insensitive, canonical spelling echoed back). Default: all statuses.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Comma list over `Vacation`, `Sick`, `Personal`, `Other` (case-insensitive, canonical spelling echoed back). Default: all types.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Optional overlap-filter range start, YYYY-MM-DD. Unlike every report endpoint, `start`/`end` are each independently optional here — see the description above.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: Optional overlap-filter range end, YYYY-MM-DD. Must be >= `start` if both are given.

parameters.name: updated_since
parameters.description: ISO 8601 timestamp with an explicit UTC offset (e.g. `Z` or `-05:00`). Returns only requests whose `COALESCE(ReviewedAt, RequestedAt)` is strictly after this instant — the delta-sync cursor for this feed.

200.description: Time-off request records matching the filters.

get.description:
Raw clock in/out and lunch punches, so an external system owns its own
overtime math instead of trusting a derived total. This is the API's
**original, stable** endpoint and does not use the shared report envelope
or the shared query-parameter contract — it predates both and its
contract is frozen.

**Delta sync** via a composite `(since, after_id)` cursor: `since` is
**required** and must be ISO 8601 with an explicit UTC offset (e.g. `Z`
or `-05:00`) — an offsetless timestamp would silently fall back to
server-default time and a delta cursor would quietly drift.  `after_id`
tie-breaks rows that share the same `updated_at` second (e.g. a batch
auto-clock-out), preventing cursor stalls. On the next poll, pass **both**
`next_since` and `next_after_id` back as `since`/`after_id` to walk the
feed without duplicates or gaps; `has_more: true` means more rows are
waiting beyond `limit`.

Unlike every other endpoint, `limit` here defaults to and caps at **500**
(not 5000), there is no `offset` (the cursor replaces it), no
`rounding`/`tz` parameter (timestamps are always rendered in
`America/Chicago`), and **no `format=csv`** — this endpoint is JSON only.

No `meta` block: like `/timeoff`, this is a raw row feed.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: ISO 8601 timestamp with an explicit UTC offset (e.g. `Z` or `-05:00`). Returns punches whose `UpdatedAt` is at or after this instant (first call inclusive with `after_id=0`).

parameters.name: after_id
parameters.description: Cursor tie-break — the `punch_id` from the previous page's `next_after_id`.

parameters.name: employee_email
parameters.description: Restrict to a single employee's punches by email (no comma-list support on this endpoint).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum punches to return. Values outside 1-500 fall back to 500 (this endpoint does not 400 on an out-of-range limit).

200.description: A page of punches plus the cursor for the next poll.

next_since.description: Pass back as `since` on the next poll. Null when no punches were returned.

next_after_id.description: Pass back as `after_id` on the next poll. Null when no punches were returned.

has_more.description: True if more punches exist beyond this page at the same `since`/`after_id`.

get.description:
The **fact table** for BI: one row per employee per **day that has punch
activity** in `[start, end]`. Every other report on this surface
(`/summary`, `/overtime`, `/utilization`) is an aggregation of these
numbers, so this is the endpoint an integrator reconciles against when a
headline figure looks wrong. Days with no punch row at all are **absent
by design** — this is a fact table, not a calendar; `/reports/attendance`
is the calendar-shaped view.

`stored_total_hours` is the raw, unsummed `timepunches.TotalHours`
column, surfaced **only for migration auditing** — never use it for math;
`worked_hours` (recomputed from the raw `TIME` columns and rounded per
the `rounding` policy) is the trustworthy figure. This report never
allocates overtime, so `week_start`/`ot_*` are not accepted.

200.description: One row per employee-day with punch activity in the range.

totals.description: Totals for the returned page only (see meta.warnings when paged).

get.description:
The headline report: one row per employee for the whole range, hours
already allocated into regular / overtime / double-time.

**Roster shaped**, unlike `/reports/hours`: every employee matching the
filters gets a row, including one who worked nothing in the range
(`days_worked: 0`, `first_punch_date: null`) — an absent row would look
like a filter mistake, a zero row looks like something to chase.

Hours are recomputed from the raw `TIME` columns, rounded once per day
per `rounding`, then allocated by `HoursCalculator::splitOvertime()` —
the **same allocator `/overtime` and `/payroll` use**, so these three
reports can never disagree about the same employee's same range.
Overtime beyond `ot_weekly` hours/week and `ot_daily` hours/day is split
out; anything past `dt_daily` (when set, and only once `ot_daily` is also
set and `dt_daily >= ot_daily`) becomes double-time.

`avg_hours_per_day` is `null` (never 0) for an employee with
`days_worked: 0` — there is no average to report, and a `0` would
quietly drag a downstream mean toward zero. If any week in the range is
partial (the range doesn't align to week boundaries), weekly overtime for
those weeks can be **understated**; `meta.warnings` says so explicitly.

200.description: One row per employee for the whole requested range.

totals.description: Totals for the returned page only (see meta.warnings when paged).

get.summary: Weekly overtime trend series per employee
get.description:
One row per employee per **week** — the series a Power BI overtime trend
chart binds to. A row exists only for a week in which the employee has at
least one punch.

Overtime is split into its **daily and weekly components** so a consumer
can see which rule produced it: `daily_overtime_hours` (from `ot_daily`/
`dt_daily`) plus `weekly_overtime_hours` (from `ot_weekly`) always sum to
`overtime_hours`, and `regular_hours + overtime_hours + double_time_hours`
always equals `worked_hours`, exactly in the published 2-decimal numbers
— both invariants are derived arithmetically from
`HoursCalculator::splitOvertime()`'s already-rounded components rather
than independently rounded, specifically so they foot in a spreadsheet.

`only_overtime=true` drops weeks with `overtime_hours + double_time_hours
<= 0` from the **rows**, but a week's partial-week flag is still raised
in `meta.warnings` even when that filter would otherwise hide it — a
partial week's overtime can be understated all the way to zero, which is
exactly the case where hiding the row would hide why.

`totals` describes the **entire filtered result**, not just the page.

parameters.name: only_overtime
parameters.description: When true, rows with no overtime or double-time are dropped. Does not suppress the partial-week warning in `meta.warnings`.

200.description: One row per employee per week with punch activity.

totals.description: Totals for the entire filtered result (not just the page).

get.description:
How much of an employee's (or an office's) schedule was actually
consumed. `group_by` selects the row shape: `employee` (default, one row
per employee for the whole range), `employee_week` (one row per
employee per week), or `office` (rolled up per office).

**Denominator rules — the part that decides whether the KPI can be
trusted:**
- `scheduled_hours` comes from the employee's one active shift, expanded
  over the days in `shifts.DaysOfWeek` that fall inside `[start, end]`,
  minus lunch, overnight-safe.
- An **approved time-off day is not scheduled capacity** — that date's
  hours move into `time_off_hours` and leave the denominator, so a week
  of approved vacation reads as "nothing scheduled," not as 0%
  utilization.
- `utilization_pct`, `overtime_pct` and `attendance_rate` are **`null`,
  never `0`, when their denominator is 0** — "we could not measure this"
  and "we measured zero" are different facts, and only `null` preserves
  the difference through a spreadsheet average (a `0` would silently
  drag a company-wide mean down).
- An employee with no active shift keeps `has_schedule: false`,
  `scheduled_days`/`scheduled_hours: 0`, and `utilization_pct: null`;
  their worked hours are still reported, but excluded from
  `totals.utilization_pct`'s denominator — see `meta.warnings` for how
  many employees this affects.

`totals.utilization_pct` is the **weighted** ratio
(`sum(worked)/sum(scheduled)` across employees who have a schedule with
hours in range), never the mean of the per-row percentages — averaging
percentages would give a part-timer scheduled 4 hours the same weight as
a full-timer scheduled 40.

`scheduled_only=true` drops employees with no active shift from the
report **entirely** (rows and totals), which is what you want for a
clean utilization KPI. `group_by=office` rows omit the per-employee
fields (`shift_name`, `has_schedule`, `attendance_rate`, `absent_days`)
and instead carry `employees`/`employees_with_schedule`.

parameters.name: group_by
parameters.description: Row shape and grouping. See the description above for what each grouping omits/adds.

parameters.name: scheduled_only
parameters.description: Drop employees with no active assigned shift entirely (rows and totals).

totals.description: Totals for the entire filtered population (not just the page); identical across all three group_by modes for the same filters.

utilization_pct.description: sum(worked)/sum(scheduled) — weighted, not a mean of row percentages. Null when no employee has scheduled hours in range.

get.summary: Attendance calendar (one row per employee per date)
get.description:
The attendance **calendar**: one row per employee per date for the whole
range, whether or not anything happened that day — an absence is the
*absence* of a punch row, so a fact-table report (`/reports/hours`) can
never count one.

`status` is exactly one of, in this precedence order: `present` (punch
activity, every punch has both ends), `incomplete` (punch activity, at
least one punch is one-sided), `time_off` (no punches, an approved
request covers the date), `absent` (no punches, no approved time off,
the date **is** scheduled), `not_scheduled` (none of the above, and the
date is **not** scheduled). Two precedence notes: punch activity outranks
time off (someone who worked an approved vacation day is `present`, with
`time_off_type` still populated so the conflict is visible); and
`time_off` outranks `not_scheduled` — an org with no shifts assigned has
no scheduled days at all, and hiding its approved leave behind
`not_scheduled` would make the status worthless there.

`minutes_late` is `first_in - shifts.StartTime` (negative = early),
`is_late` applies that shift's own `GracePeriodMinutes`; both are `null`
when the employee was not scheduled that day — "late" has no meaning
without a scheduled start.

**Size**: the grid is employees × dates, so 400 days over a 100-person
roster is 40,000 rows. `total_count` is the true size of the filtered
grid; `meta.grid` reports the **unfiltered** employees × dates size so an
integrator can see how much `status`/`scheduled_only` trimmed. `totals`
describes the entire filtered result, not the returned page.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Comma list over `present`, `incomplete`, `time_off`, `absent`, `not_scheduled`. Default: all.

parameters.name: scheduled_only
parameters.description: Only emit rows for dates the employee was actually scheduled to work.

200.description: One row per employee per date in the range.

totals.description: Totals for the entire filtered result (not just the page).

get.summary: Time-off request analytics, apportioned and optionally folded up
get.description:
Time-off analytics: the requests themselves, or folded up per employee /
per employee-and-type, via `group_by`. This is the aggregated counterpart
to the raw `/timeoff` feed.

**Range semantics — the part that decides whether two adjacent pulls
double count:** a request is *in* the range when it **overlaps** it
(`StartDate <= end AND EndDate >= start`), not when it is contained by
it — a vacation starting in March and ending in April belongs to both
months' reports. Every request row therefore carries both
`days_requested`/`hours_requested` (the full span) and
`days_in_range`/`hours_in_range` (the span **clipped** to
`[start, end]`); summing `hours_requested` across two adjacent ranges
double counts a straddling request, summing `hours_in_range` does not
— and the aggregate groupings (`group_by=employee`/`employee_type`)
total the **clipped** figures for exactly this reason.

**Hours source, two different rules:** an **approved** request prices
each in-range date at that employee's scheduled hours for the date
(0 on a non-working day or for an unscheduled employee) — the same rule
`/reports/utilization` uses for its denominator, so the two reports can
never disagree about how much leave a day consumed; `HoursRequested` is
trusted only on a single-day request. **Pending/Rejected** requests never
reached the schedule, so they simply apportion `HoursRequested` by
calendar days in range instead.

`totals` describe the **returned page**, not the full filtered result
(unlike most other reports here) — `meta.warnings` says so whenever the
result is paged.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Comma list over `Pending`, `Approved`, `Rejected`. Default: all.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Comma list over `Vacation`, `Sick`, `Personal`, `Other`. Default: all.

parameters.name: group_by
parameters.description: `request` emits one row per request (with reviewer/reason detail); `employee` folds all matching requests up per employee, split by status and leave type; `employee_type` folds up per (employee, leave type) pair.

totals.description: Totals for the returned page only.

rules.approved_hours: HoursRequested on a single-day request, otherwise the employee's scheduled hours for each date in range
rules.pending_rejected_hours: HoursRequested apportioned by calendar days in range

get.summary: Current leave balances by employee and type
get.description:
Current leave balances: one row per employee per leave type for a single
year. **Point-in-time** — this report deliberately does **not** take
`start`/`end`: a balance is a running ledger figure, not something that
accrues inside a window.

`available_hours = accrued + carryover - used` and is **not clamped** —
an employee who took leave they had not accrued really is negative, and
clamping would hide the exception a BI consumer is looking for;
`is_negative` flags those rows so a spreadsheet can filter on a boolean
instead of a sign test.

An employee with no ledger row for `year` produces **no row** — a
fabricated all-zero row would be indistinguishable from a real zeroed
balance, and the two mean very different things (never enrolled vs.
fully consumed). `include_zero=true` keeps rows that genuinely exist and
are all-zero (excluded by default). `policy_*` columns come from the
(possibly deactivated) accrual policy and are `null` when no policy row
exists for that leave type.

`totals` describe the **returned page**, not the full filtered result.

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: 4-digit year. Default is the current year in the report timezone.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Comma list over `Vacation`, `Sick`, `Personal`, `Other`. Default: all.

parameters.name: include_zero
parameters.description: Keep ledger rows whose accrued, carryover and used hours are all 0.

200.description: One row per employee per leave type for the requested year.

totals.description: Totals for the returned page only.

rules.policy_source: leave_accrual_policy joined on LeaveType, not filtered by IsActive
rules.row_source: existing leave_balances rows only; an employee with no ledger row for the year is not represented

get.summary: Payroll-ready hours for a pay period
get.description:
One row per employee for the requested pay period, shaped to hand
straight to payroll / QuickBooks: worked hours split into regular /
overtime / double-time, approved time off broken out by category, and
the paid total.

**Roster shaped**: a row is emitted for every employee matching the
filter, even one with no punches and no time off — payroll needs to see
the zero. Narrow the population with `employee_id`/`office` to get only
people who actually worked.

Row invariants, true in the **published 2-decimal numbers**:
`regular_hours + overtime_hours + double_time_hours == total_worked_hours`;
`vacation_hours + sick_hours + personal_hours + other_timeoff_hours ==
total_timeoff_hours`; `total_worked_hours + total_timeoff_hours ==
total_paid_hours`. Weekly overtime is bucketed by calendar week **inside**
the period, so a pay period that doesn't align to week boundaries carries
the standard partial-week understatement warning.
`include_timeoff=false` reports every time-off column as `0` (not
computed) and `total_paid_hours` then equals `total_worked_hours`.

`totals` describes the **entire filtered result**, not just the page.

parameters.name: include_timeoff
parameters.description: When false, time-off columns report 0 and are not computed at all.

200.description: One row per employee for the requested pay period.

totals.description: Totals for the entire filtered result (not just the page).

get.description:
Payroll-prep data quality: the punch records that will make payroll
**wrong** if they go out uncorrected.

**One row per detected problem**, not per employee and not per punch — a
single punch can legitimately raise several exceptions at once (a
19-hour punch with half a lunch is both `excessive_shift` and
`incomplete_lunch`), each with a different fix. `exception_id` is
`"<type>:<punch_id>"`, unique and stable across runs.

**Types and their fixed severity** (a property of the type, never of the
row): `high` — `missing_clock_out`, `overlapping_punch`,
`negative_duration`; `medium` — `excessive_shift`, `zero_hours`,
`incomplete_lunch`; `low` — `missing_clock_in`, `no_lunch_long_shift`,
`unscheduled_day`, `future_punch`.

**The rule that decides whether this report is usable:** an open punch
dated **today** is a person currently on the clock, not an exception —
`missing_clock_out` requires the punch date to be strictly before today
in the report timezone, or every working employee would appear on the
report every morning.

`long_shift_hours` (default 16, 0 disables) and `no_lunch_threshold`
(default 6, 0 disables) tune two of the ten detectors; the other eight
have no threshold to tune. Punches from one day either side of the range
are read as **overlap partners only** — they never raise exceptions of
their own — so an overnight punch at the range boundary is still checked
correctly; widen the range to actually inspect them.

`totals` describe the **entire filtered result**, not the returned page.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Comma list over `missing_clock_out`, `overlapping_punch`, `negative_duration`, `excessive_shift`, `zero_hours`, `incomplete_lunch`, `missing_clock_in`, `no_lunch_long_shift`, `unscheduled_day`, `future_punch`. Default: all.

parameters.name: severity
parameters.description: Comma list over `high`, `medium`, `low`. Default: all.

parameters.name: long_shift_hours
parameters.description: Hours above which a single punch raises `excessive_shift`. 0 disables the check.

parameters.name: no_lunch_threshold
parameters.description: Hours worked with no lunch recorded that raises `no_lunch_long_shift`. 0 disables the check.

200.description: One row per detected data-quality exception.

totals.description: Totals for the entire filtered result (not just the page).

by_type.description: Count per exception type. Every type key is always present, including zeros.

by_severity.description: Count per severity. Always has high/medium/low keys.

rows.detail: Clocked in 07:58 with no clock-out; punch is 4 day(s) old and contributes 0 paid hours until it is closed.
rows.suggested_action: Add a clock-out or delete the punch

rules.open_punch_grace: a punch dated today with no clock-out is treated as work in progress, not as a missing clock-out

warnings: This report only examines punches dated 2026-08-17 to 2026-08-23. A punch left open before 2026-08-17 will not appear here. Widen the range to find it.

get.description:
Arrival/departure behaviour per employee over the range, measured
against each employee's own scheduled shift.

**Requires an active assigned shift.** An employee with none is excluded
**entirely** — not emitted with nulls, not counted in totals — because
there is no scheduled start to measure lateness against; how many were
excluded is stated in `meta.warnings`.

A **measured day** is a scheduled date on which the employee has a punch
with a usable clock-in. A scheduled day with no punch at all is an
*absence*, not a punctuality data point, and does not enter
`days_worked` or any rate derived from it.

`minutes_late = first_in − shift.StartTime`. `late` means
`minutes_late > GracePeriodMinutes` (the shift's own authoritative grace
window); `early` means more than 5 minutes before start; everything else
(including up to the grace period late, or up to 5 minutes early) is
`on_time`. Early departure mirrors this with the **same** 5-minute
buffer applied to `shift.EndTime` (there is no separate departure
threshold — reusing the arrival number is documented here, not silently
assumed). `first_in_median` is the **median**, not the mean, arrival
time — one very early or very late outlier must not drag a "typical
arrival time" around.

`totals` describe the entire filtered population, never just the page.

200.description: One row per employee with an active assigned shift.

totals.description: Totals for the entire filtered population (not just the page).

worst_offender.description: The employee with the highest late_rate among those with at least one measured day, or null if none qualify.

rules.late_threshold: minutes_late > shift GracePeriodMinutes (per employee — see each row's grace_period_minutes)

get.summary: Gap-free time series for trend charts
get.description:
Time series for BI trending — the endpoint a Power BI line chart binds
to directly. One row per interval bucket (`day`/`week`/`month`),
optionally split by employee or office via `group_by`.

**Gap-free series** is the entire reason this endpoint exists rather
than "just filter `/summary` by week": every bucket in `[start, end]`
gets a row, including buckets with zero activity, and (when grouped)
every employee/office in the filtered roster gets a row for every
bucket, including one where they did nothing. A chart binding to a query
that silently omits empty periods draws a misleading straight line
across a gap instead of a real drop to zero.

**`interval=day`**: `overtime_hours` reflects only the **daily**
thresholds (`ot_daily`/`dt_daily`) — a weekly overtime hour cannot be
pinned to one day, so it is excluded from day-level rows entirely rather
than mislabeled (see `meta.warnings`). **`interval=week`**: weekly
overtime is exactly what the underlying structure reports — no
ambiguity. **`interval=month`**: the unambiguous daily pieces are summed
by the calendar month the day falls in; the weekly-threshold component of
each week is attributed **whole** to the month containing that week's
**start** date, which can shift a small number of overtime hours across
a month boundary relative to a strict per-day allocation (flagged in
`meta.warnings` only when it actually happens in range).

`totals` (periods, employees, worked/regular/overtime hours) describes
the entire filtered population over the whole range, computed once from
the whole-range weekly split — independent of `interval` and of paging,
so it is never subject to the day/month attribution caveats above.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: Bucket size. See the description above for the overtime attribution caveat on each.

parameters.name: group_by
parameters.description: Split each bucket by employee or office, or leave company-wide (none).

200.description: One row per bucket (optionally per employee/office per bucket).

totals.description: Whole-range, whole-population totals, independent of interval and of paging.

warnings: interval=day: overtime_hours (and regular_hours) reflect only the DAILY overtime/double-time thresholds (ot_daily/dt_daily).

get.description:
GPS compliance: punches recorded outside their geofence.

**One row per event, not per punch**: a single punch can carry up to
four independently-captured coordinate pairs (`clock_in`, `lunch_start`,
`lunch_end`, `clock_out`), each its own GPS fix with its own accuracy and
its own compliance verdict. Folding them into one row per punch would
force an arbitrary "worst of four" choice this endpoint has no business
making. Only events that actually have coordinates produce a row.

**No active geofence configured** → the whole report is meaningless (there
is nothing to be outside of), so it returns an **empty, successful**
result with a `meta.warnings` entry saying so — not a misleading
all-clean 0 and not an error.

**Violation definition**: `distance > radius` of the *nearest* active
geofence (Haversine, kept as the minimum over every active geofence — an
employee near two sites is judged against the one they're actually
closest to) when `source=computed`; or the stored app verdict
(`!GeofencePass*`) when `source=stored` (this install currently has no
such data — every row is `source=computed`, see `meta.warnings`).
`min_meters_outside` is a severity floor that applies **only** to
`source=computed` rows — a `source=stored` violation always qualifies,
since this endpoint's own distance can legitimately disagree with the
app's stored verdict (a different geofence set, a since-moved fence) and
using it to discard the app's verdict could hide a real violation.
`max_accuracy` excludes readings too imprecise to judge either way
(excluded from consideration, not counted as compliant); a `null`
accuracy (never recorded) is **not** excluded — there is no evidence it
was bad, only no evidence at all.

`only_violations=false` returns every checked event, compliant ones
included, regardless of `min_meters_outside` — nothing needed for a
compliance-rate chart is silently dropped by a threshold meant only to
reduce violation noise.

parameters.name: only_violations
parameters.description: When false, every checked event is returned, compliant ones included.

parameters.name: min_meters_outside
parameters.description: Severity floor on distance-outside-geofence. Applies only to source=computed rows — see the description above.

parameters.name: max_accuracy
parameters.description: Drop readings whose reported GPS accuracy is worse (numerically larger) than this many meters. 0 disables the filter.

200.description: One row per checked GPS event (violations only, by default).

totals.description: Totals for the entire filtered result (not just the page).

warnings: This install has no GeofencePass* columns; every row was computed here via Haversine distance rather than read from a stored app verdict (source=computed on every row).

ApiKeyBearer.description:
Server-to-server API key authentication for `/api/external/v1/*`. Send
`Authorization: Bearer <key>` where `<key>` is exactly **64 lowercase
hexadecimal characters** (`^[a-f0-9]{64}$`) — any other shape, a missing
header, or a malformed `Authorization` value is rejected as a uniform
`401 Invalid API key` (the response never distinguishes "missing,"
"malformed" and "revoked/expired," so a client cannot enumerate key
lifecycle state).

**Keys are created in Admin → API Keys**, where an administrator grants
one or more scopes at creation time (`employees:read`, `offices:read`,
`punches:read`, `reports:read`, `shifts:read`, `timeoff:read` — see the
scope catalog referenced by each operation's `x-required-scope`).
Calling an endpoint without the scope it requires returns `403`.

**Rate limit: 60 requests/minute per key**, a sliding one-minute window.
Exceeding it returns `429` with a `Retry-After: 60` header. A separate,
IP-scoped throttle (20 failed auth attempts / 15 minutes) applies before
the key is even parsed, to slow down key-guessing; that throttle also
returns `429` (`Retry-After: 900`) and is keyed by client IP, not by key.

start.name: start
start.description: Inclusive range start, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Required together with `end` whenever an operation accepts it. `end` must be on or after `start`, and the inclusive span between them may not exceed 400 days.

end.name: end
end.description: Inclusive range end, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Must be on or after `start`; the range may span at most 400 days.

employee_id.name: employee_id
employee_id.description: One positive integer employee ID, or a comma-separated list (e.g. `3,7,11`). Any value that is not a positive integer returns `400`.

employee_email.name: employee_email
employee_email.description: One employee email address, or a comma-separated list. Each value must be a valid email of at most 255 characters, or the request returns `400`.

office.name: office
office.description: One office name, or a comma-separated list. Matched against `users.Office` (and, where relevant, `Offices.OfficeName`) using the column's own case-insensitive collation; each value is limited to 100 characters. Does not need to correspond to a row in the offices lookup table — see `GET /offices` for how an orphaned office name is reported.

include_inactive.name: include_inactive
include_inactive.description: Include locked-out ("inactive") employees in the result. Defaults to **false** on every report/dimension endpoint that accepts it. The one exception is `GET /employees`, which defaults to **true** for backward compatibility — see that operation's description.

rounding.name: rounding
rounding.description: Rounding interval in minutes, applied once to each employee's summed DAY before overtime is allocated. `0` disables rounding. No other integer is accepted — an out-of-list value returns `400` naming the accepted set.

week_start.name: week_start
week_start.description: First day of the work week, for bucketing weekly overtime and week-shaped rows.

ot_weekly.name: ot_weekly
ot_weekly.description: Weekly overtime threshold in hours. `0` disables weekly overtime entirely.

ot_daily.name: ot_daily
ot_daily.description: Daily overtime threshold in hours. `0` (the default) disables daily overtime.

dt_daily.name: dt_daily
dt_daily.description: Daily double-time threshold in hours. `0` (the default) disables double-time. When both `dt_daily` and `ot_daily` are set (nonzero), `dt_daily` must be greater than or equal to `ot_daily`, or the request returns `400`.

tz.name: tz
tz.description: An IANA timezone name (e.g. `America/New_York`, `UTC`) all timestamps in the response are rendered in, and that resolves relative concepts like "today" for that request. Default, in order: this installation's branding timezone, then `DB_TIMEZONE`, then `America/Chicago`.

format.name: format
format.description: Response format. `csv` streams `data.rows` as a UTF-8 CSV (with BOM) instead of the JSON envelope; `meta`/`totals` have no CSV representation and are mirrored into `X-Report-*` response headers instead. Not honored by `GET /punches` (JSON only) and has no effect on `GET /meta` (nothing tabular to export).

limit.name: limit
limit.description: Maximum rows to return. Values outside 1-5000 return `400`.

offset.name: offset
offset.description: Rows to skip before the returned page. Capped at 1,000,000 (a deep offset is a performance trap even below that).

Envelope.description: The outer shape of every JSON response on this API, success or error.

data.description: Endpoint-specific payload. See each operation's response schema for the concrete shape.

Pagination.description: The pagination fields present on every report/dimension endpoint's `meta` block.

limit.description: The effective `limit` applied to this request.

offset.description: The effective `offset` applied to this request.

row_count.description: Number of rows in this page.

total_count.description: Number of rows in the full filtered result. On most reports this spans the entire filtered result set regardless of paging; a few endpoints (noted in their own description) scope totals/total_count to the returned page instead — check meta.warnings, which always says so when it applies.

Meta.description: The `meta` block returned alongside every row-listing response. Some report endpoints append extra report-specific keys on top of the fields documented here — most commonly additional entries under `filters` (e.g. utilization's `group_by`) — see each operation's description for what is specific to it.

generated_at.description: When this response was generated, in the response timezone.

timezone.description: The IANA timezone every timestamp in this response is rendered in.

start.description: Effective range start, or null for an endpoint that does not take one.

end.description: Effective range end, or null for an endpoint that does not take one.

filters.description: The effective filters applied (employee_id, employee_email, office, include_inactive, plus any report-specific filters).

rules.description: The effective rounding/overtime/report-specific rules applied to the numbers in this response.

ignored_params.description: Query parameter names this endpoint does not honor, echoed back so a typo (e.g. "employe_id") is visible instead of silently ignored.

warnings.description: Plain-English caveats about this specific response (partial weeks, open punches, a paged total, an unmeasurable employee, etc.). Always check before trusting a headline number.

MetaInfo.description: The `data` payload of `GET /meta` — API discovery info.

endpoints.description: Hand-maintained catalog of every endpoint that actually exists today (authoritative over any inference from a scope name).

Error.description: The error envelope returned on every non-2xx response.

error.description: Plain-English error message. Validation errors name the offending parameter and what is accepted.

errors.description: Optional structured detail for a multi-field validation failure. Not used by any GET-only endpoint on this surface today.

CsvExport.description: UTF-8 CSV with a leading BOM, one header row, and one row per result (formula-injection-safe: a cell starting with =, +, -, @, tab or CR is quoted). `meta`/`totals` are not representable in CSV and are mirrored into `X-Report-Timezone`, `X-Report-Row-Count`, `X-Report-Total-Count`, `X-Report-Has-More` and (when present) `X-Report-Warnings` response headers instead.

EmployeeRow.description: One employee on the roster. Legacy field names/types (`id` as a string) are preserved for backward compatibility — see GET /employees.

id.description: Employee ID as a string (legacy contract — every other endpoint uses an integer employee_id).

active.description: True unless the employee is locked out.

office_id.description: ID of the matching Offices row, or null when users.Office has no match there.

shift_id.description: Active assigned shift ID, or null with no active assignment.

has_schedule.description: True iff shift_id is not null.

clock_status.description: Internal 'Lunch' status folds into 'In'. Null means never punched (distinct from Out).

office_id.description: Null when this office_name exists only as free text on users.Office with no matching Offices row (an orphan — see meta.warnings).

end_time.description: HH:MM:SS. At or before start_time means the shift crosses midnight.

days_of_week.description: Empty when DaysOfWeek failed to decode or named no recognized day — see meta.warnings for which shifts this affects.

scheduled_hours_per_day.description: Span minus lunch, for one day of this shift; not date-specific.

active_assigned_employee_count.description: Subset of assigned_employee_count that is not locked out.

scheduled_hours.description: Reported even on a date covered by approved time off — see is_working_day.

is_working_day.description: False when an approved time-off request covers this date.

days.description: Inclusive day count; 0 if start_date/end_date is an unusable legacy sentinel.

reviewed_by.description: Null when never reviewed, or the reviewing admin account was since deleted.

external_employee_id.description: The employee's ID, as a string (matches the legacy /employees.id contract).

clock_out.description: Null when the punch is still open.

worked_hours.description: Recomputed from raw TIME columns and rounded per `rounding` — never timepunches.TotalHours.

span_hours.description: last_out minus first_in, unrounded, ignoring lunch.

stored_total_hours.description: Raw timepunches.TotalHours, for migration audit ONLY — do not use for math.

UtilizationRow.description: Shape varies by `group_by`. `employee`/`employee_week` rows carry employee_id/employee_email/employee_name/job_title/shift_name/ has_schedule/attendance_rate/absent_days; employee_week rows additionally carry week_start/week_end/is_partial_week. `office` rows instead carry office/employees/employees_with_schedule and omit the per-employee-only fields. All fields below are declared optional/nullable to cover every variant — see the operation description for exactly which fields each group_by populates.

office.description: The employee's office (employee/employee_week rows), or the office name itself (office rows).

utilization_pct.description: Null, never 0, when scheduled_hours is 0 for this row.

attendance_rate.description: employee/employee_week only. Can exceed 100 (an unscheduled day worked).

minutes_late.description: first_in minus scheduled start, minutes. Null when not scheduled.

minutes_early_departure.description: Null when not scheduled, no clock-out yet, or the punch is still open.

notes_present.description: Whether a punch note exists — the note's CONTENT is never exposed by this report.

TimeoffReportRow.description: Shape varies by `group_by`. `request` rows carry the full request detail (request_id/status/dates/reviewer). `employee` rows fold every matching request up per employee with a status/type breakdown. `employee_type` rows fold up per (employee, leave type) pair. All fields below are optional/nullable to cover every variant.

days_requested.description: request and employee rows: full span (request) or clipped sum (employee).

days_in_range.description: request rows only — span clipped to [start, end].

hours_in_range.description: request rows only — the clipped, priced figure.

available_hours.description: accrued + carryover - used. NOT clamped to 0 — can be negative.

severity.description: A property of the type, never of the individual row.

worked_hours.description: Null when no computable duration (e.g. missing an end).

detail.description: Human-readable explanation of this specific occurrence.

days_worked.description: Measured days only — a scheduled day with no punch is an absence, not counted here.

avg_minutes_late.description: Mean over LATE days only. Null when late_days is 0.

total_minutes_late.description: 0.0 (not null) when there are no late days — a real fact, unlike the null averages above.

first_in_median.description: Median (not mean) first-clock-in time, HH:MM, over measured days.

TrendRow.description: Shape varies by `group_by`. `none` rows are company-wide per bucket; `employee` rows add employee_id/employee_name; `office` rows add office. All fields below are optional/nullable to cover every variant.

period_label.description: Chart-axis label, e.g. "2026-08-03" (day), an ISO week label (week), or "2026-08" (month).

is_partial.description: True when this bucket's calendar span extends outside [start, end] — only possible at the range edges.

employees_active.description: Employees with any punch in this bucket (open punches count as active).

overtime_hours.description: Attribution depends on `interval` — see the operation description.

accuracy_meters.description: Reported GPS accuracy in meters. Null means never recorded (not treated as bad).

nearest_geofence.description: Name of the nearest ACTIVE geofence by Haversine distance, not necessarily the intended one.

meters_outside.description: geofence_distance_meters minus geofence_radius_meters. Negative means inside the geofence.

source.description: "stored" = the app's own recorded verdict; "computed" = derived here via Haversine distance because no stored verdict exists on this install.

BadRequest.description: A query parameter failed validation. `error` names the offending parameter and what is accepted.

example.error: Invalid parameter `rounding`: "7". Accepted values are 0, 5, 6, 10, 15, 20, 30 (minutes; 0 disables rounding).

Unauthorized.description: Missing, malformed, revoked or expired API key. The message is uniform across all four cases so a client cannot enumerate key lifecycle state.

Forbidden.description: The API key is valid but lacks the scope this endpoint requires.

MethodNotAllowed.description: Every endpoint on this API is GET-only.

example.error: Method not allowed. This endpoint accepts: GET.

TooManyRequests.description: Either the per-key rate limit (60 requests/minute) or the per-IP failed-auth throttle (20 failures/15 minutes) was exceeded.

schema.description: Seconds until the limit resets — 60 for the per-key rate limit, 900 for the failed-auth throttle.

example.error: Rate limit exceeded (60 requests/min per key)

InternalServerError.description: An unexpected server-side failure. Logged server-side with the exception class, message, file and line; never exposed to the client.
